rationale: The assistant immediately told the customer to stop resetting the RCD and stop using the machine, and ended by correctly directing them to an appliance engineer. The element diagnosis is reasonable but stated as 'classic' and 'most likely' without an insulation test, and the second message wrongly repeated a boilerplate burning-smell warning even though the customer had reported no smell. It also asked the customer to do a continuity test they could not safely do, and never asked which RCD tripped or whether it also trips on another circuit, so it did not use the cross-circuit evidence or ask for the model number. It did not name a part to buy and correctly did not blame the house wiring, though it said an electrician would not test the machine, which misses the electrician fallback if the trip continues with the machine unplugged.
